title: Appeal Terms for Denied Delivery Claims
content:
A denied Delivery Claims claim can be appealed at most the claim type's number of appeals — one appeal per claim under every claim type. An appeal is accepted only if it is made no later than the claim type's appeal window in calendar days after the claim is decided. The decision date is day zero and the last day of the window still counts. Where the claim type requires new evidence, at least one evidence item must have been logged on the claim after the decision date; repeating the original account is not an appeal.

## Conditions of an appeal

| Condition | Read from |
|---|---|
| the claim is denied | the claim's status |
| no earlier appeal on the claim, under the limit of one | the appeals recorded on the claim |
| made within the window counted from the decision date | the claim's decision date |
| at least one evidence item logged after the decision date | the dates of the evidence entries on the claim |

An accepted appeal returns the claim from denied to under review and adds one to the appeals recorded on it.

## Window boundary (hypothetical dates, window of 30 calendar days)

| Decision date | Last day an appeal is accepted | First day it is not |
|---|---|---|
| 5 May | 4 June | 5 June |
| 20 October | 19 November | 20 November |

## Points of judgement

- *Hypothetical:* a customer calls within the window and restates that the parcel never arrived, with nothing new logged since the denial. That is a repetition of the original account, not an appeal.
- *Hypothetical:* a police report reference logged two days after the decision date is evidence logged after the decision date and satisfies the new-evidence condition.
- *Hypothetical:* a claim already appealed once and denied again cannot be appealed a second time.
